messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@medsure.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: MedSure IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, and BCP/DR artifacts

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap: we covered scope for a potential pilot (500k tokens/mo, production latency SLOs), data residency (US-only), and initial security checklist items (SOC 2, breach notif, BAA). You mentioned an internal security review next week and legal will ask about a BAA.

2) IR / breach notification: for procurement and for our internal playbooks, could you confirm MedSure's expected notification SLA for incidents that may involve PHI or customer-identifiable data? Specifically: 
- Required notification window after detection (we typically plan for 72 hours but can support faster escalation).
- Responsible contacts and escalation hierarchy (email + phone).

3) Evidence request (to move the security review along):
- Current SOC 2 status (Type II if available) and the date range of the most recent report. If the full report is restricted, a SOC 2 summary or assertion PDF is fine.
- High-level IR runbook or tabletop playbook (we only need the overview / process map, redacted items OK).
- BCP/DR RTO and RPO targets for production services.
- Any specific GDPR/HIPAA controls we should be aware of for onboarding.

4) Vendor questionnaire: if you prefer, we can send our brief vendor questionnaire (6–8 targeted items) instead of the longer security intake. Indicate preferred format (Doc link, encrypted email, or DocuSign/Sharepoint upload).

5) Next meeting: propose a 30m sync next Wed 12/2 to review the SOC2 status and agree on IR timelines. If legal needs a BAA before that, we can loop in our compliance lead.

I attached a short SOC2/evidence checklist and an anonymized sample audit log export to show the fields we typically ask for (filename stubs below).

Attachments (stubs): SOC2-summary-2025.pdf; audit_logs_sample-202611.csv

Thanks — Kim
--

From: Sara Thomas <sara.thomas@medsure.com>

Kim — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Quick answers to help you prep: 

- SOC 2: MedSure has a SOC 2 Type II report for calendar 2025; the full report is restricted to partners under NDA but I can send a redacted summary (we provided that to several vendors last quarter).

- Breach notif SLA: our policy is to notify affected partners within 72 hours of confirmed detection for incidents involving PHI/customer-identifiable data. For incidents with unknown impact we aim to send an initial notification within 24 hours stating we are investigating.

- Contacts: security_ops@medsure.com is our primary intake; escalation to myself and our CISO (robert.hale@medsure.com) for severity >= P2. I will include a short contact table in my next note.

- BCP/DR: Our RTO for core customer-facing APIs is 4 hours, RPO is 1 hour. We have a secondary region (us-west) failover and annual tabletop tests; I can provide the executive summary of the plan.

- HIPAA/GDPR: We are HIPAA-covered for PHI; GDPR applies to EU-subject data (not in scope for your current US-only pilot but we will flag any cross-border items).

Prefer to receive the vendor questionnaire as a secured Doc link or via DocuSign. I will try to share the SOC2-summary and BCP exec summary by EOD tomorrow.

- Log retention ask: we can support configurable retention; need to map which stream(s) you require 5 years for (access logs vs. application logs). We typically keep access token logs for 90 days by default and can export to customer-managed storage for long-term retention.

- IR runbook: attaching our IR_runbook_redwood_v1.docx (redacted runbook overview + escalation matrix) and a short SOC2 request checklist to streamline your upload. The audit_logs_sample-202611.csv I shared yesterday is the shape of logs we can produce on export.

Kim / Sara — quick note from infra: we can export audit logs to an S3 bucket in us-west with lifecycle rules for 5-year retention (objects archived to Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days). There is a modest monthly storage cost; for a rough ballpark: ~ $120/month for 1TB retained in Glacier Deep Archive (subject to compression/encryption).

We also support a push of critical access logs via secure syslog to customer endpoints with a TLS + mTLS handshake. I'll include details in the calendar invite.
